title: Servicing Provider, Military Clinic First Refusal and Access Settings in Referrals and Authorizations
content:
Network management sets, for each **Referrals and Authorizations** type, who may serve the patient, whether a military hospital or clinic gets the right of first refusal on a TRICARE Prime request, whether the patient may move the authorization to another servicing provider, and the access standards the servicing provider is held to.

| Authorization type | Military clinic right of first refusal on a Prime request | Business days the military clinic has to accept or decline | Patient may move the authorization to another servicing provider | Kinds of provider that may serve | Appointment offered within (calendar days, access standard) | Maximum drive time (minutes, access standard) | Region books the first appointment on approval |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Specialty Care Referral | yes | 2 | yes | network specialist; military hospital or clinic | 28 | 60 | yes |
| Rehabilitative Therapy Referral | yes | 2 | yes | network specialist; military hospital or clinic | 28 | 60 | yes |
| Durable Medical Equipment Authorization | no | 0 | yes | network facility | 0 | 0 | no |
| Home Health Care Authorization | no | 0 | yes | network facility | 0 | 0 | no |
| Applied Behavior Analysis Authorization | no | 0 | yes | network specialist | 28 | 60 | no |
| Skilled Nursing Facility Authorization | no | 0 | no | network facility | 0 | 0 | no |
| Inpatient Mental Health Authorization | yes | 1 | no | network facility; military hospital or clinic | 0 | 0 | no |

## Reading the settings

- A figure of 0 in the access columns means no access standard applies to that type.
- Three types give the military clinic the right of first refusal: the Specialty Care Referral and the Rehabilitative Therapy Referral, with 2 business days to answer, and the Inpatient Mental Health Authorization, with 1 business day.
- The two inpatient types cannot be moved to another servicing provider at the patient's request.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A Specialty Care Referral approved to a network specialist must, under the access standard, be met by an appointment offer within 28 calendar days and a drive time of no more than 60 minutes.
